cbv24:2.1: Then the yakkha Ālavaka recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
cbv24:4.1: thus, after passing from this world to the next world, one does not grieve.
cbv24:6.1: After saying this, the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
cbv24:8.1: Just as, reverend Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned,
cbv24:8.2: or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost,
cbv24:8.3: or bear an oil lamp in the darkness so that one who has eyes can see forms,
cbv24:8.4: just so has the Dhamma been made clear by reverend Gotama in more than one way.
cbv24:9.1: I go to the reverend Gotama for refuge,
cbv24:9.2: and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
cbv24:10.1: Please bear it in mind, reverend Gotama, that I am a lay disciple
cbv24:10.2: who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life.”
